claims.claim: Born 7 May 1998 in Wichita, Kansas
claims.note: Britannica Quick Facts: May 7, 1998, Wichita, Kansas.

claims.claim: Passed 500 million YouTube subscribers on 12 June 2026
claims.note: Now reads "in June 2026". The YouTube blog is dated 12 June 2026 and reports the milestone as already reached, so June 2026 is supported.

claims.claim: First individual creator to reach 500 million subscribers
claims.note: YouTube: 'the first individual creator to reach 500 million subscribers on YouTube'.

claims.claim: Raised in Greenville, North Carolina; moved often; cared for by au pairs
claims.note: Page says primarily raised in Greenville, NC; au pairs due to parents' long hours and military service.

claims.claim: Parents divorced in 2007
claims.note: Page states the divorce year.

claims.claim: Graduated Greenville Christian Academy in 2016; briefly attended Pitt Community College and dropped out
claims.note: Matches page.

claims.claim: First YouTube upload February 2012 at age 13
claims.note: Page: 'at the age of 13', under the name MrBeast6000.

claims.claim: Most-subscribed individual creator in November 2022; most-subscribed channel in June 2024
claims.note: Both dates stated by YouTube.

claims.claim: Adweek: about 1.3 billion unique viewers each quarter, roughly 80% outside the US, top video approaching 950 million views, figures attributed to CEO Jeff Housenbold
claims.note: Adweek attributes these figures to Housenbold 'according to' him. The article correctly calls them company figures.

claims.claim: #TeamTrees raised over $25 million for a campaign that aimed to plant more than 25 million trees
claims.note: Reworded to "aimed to plant", which matches YouTube.

claims.claim: #TeamSeas raised more than $30 million for ocean and beach cleanup
claims.note: YouTube: 'raised more than $30 million to remove trash from beaches, rivers and the ocean'.

claims.claim: #TeamWater in 2025 with Mark Rober drew creators from 115 countries and raised about $40 million for WaterAid
claims.note: 115 countries refers to creators, which the article says.

claims.claim: '50 YouTubers Fight for $1,000,000' and April 2026 livestreamed sequel '50 Streamers Fight for $1,000,000'
claims.note: Named as massive creator events; no outcome or date stated, and the article states none.

claims.claim: Feastables introduced January 2022 with MrBeast Bar in three flavors; about $10 million in sales in first few months
claims.note: Wikipedia says so. Feastables About page gives no founding year or revenue, and the article says so. Wikipedia is only a research lead under the style guide, so consider a primary source.

claims.claim: Feastables mission to eradicate child labor in cocoa; 100% Fairtrade cocoa; farmers paid living income reference price or market price, whichever higher; better-for-you snack company
claims.note: Matches the About page wording and is presented as company claims.

claims.claim: Beast Industries is a conglomerate Donaldson founded that holds various media channels
claims.note: Matches page.

claims.claim: Jeff Housenbold is CEO of Beast Industries
claims.note: Adweek identifies him as CEO.

claims.claim: January 2026 Bitmine agreed to invest $200 million in Beast Industries, led by chairman Tom Lee; Lee calls MrBeast the leading content creator of their generation
claims.note: DL News: announced 15 January 2026; Lee's 'in our view' remark; chairman per press release attribution.

claims.claim: Investment valued the company at $5 billion (Wikipedia); DL News says valuation not disclosed
claims.note: Wikipedia gives $5 billion at the $200M raise. DL News says the valuation was not disclosed. The article flags the conflict.

claims.claim: Hosts Beast Games and co-created it
claims.note: Credited as host, co-creator and executive producer.

claims.claim: First season released on Prime Video on 19 December 2024
claims.note: Amazon: premiere December 19, 2024.

claims.claim: Most-watched unscripted series reaching 50 million viewers 25 days after premiere
claims.note: Amazon: streaming service's most-watched unscripted show ever; 50M viewers 25 days after premiere.

claims.claim: Renewed for two more seasons on 12 May 2025 at Amazon's upfront in New York
claims.note: Amazon page; year from metadata dated 2025-05-12.

claims.claim: Vernon Sanders, Amazon MGM Studios head of television, called it 'the largest reality competition series ever'
claims.note: Exact quote and title confirmed.

claims.claim: Fortune reported in January 2026 that he is projected to be worth at least $2.6 billion; no named estimator; no as-of date
claims.note: Article says 'projected to be worth at least $2.6 billion', names no estimator and gives no as-of date.

claims.claim: Forbes estimated annual earnings of $85 million from April 2024 to April 2025
claims.note: Fortune cites this Forbes estimate.

claims.claim: WSJ quotes: 'I'm borrowing money. That's how little money I have' and 'I have negative money right now'
claims.note: Quotes appear in the Fortune piece.

claims.claim: Keeps less than $1 million for himself; reinvests in businesses
claims.note: Article attributes the under $1M remark to earlier People coverage and cites an X post on reinvestment.

claims.claim: Married Thea Booysen in 2026
claims.note: Dexerto: confirmed 21 July 2026.

claims.claim: 11 July 2026 post: 'may or may not be getting married'
claims.note: Quoted in Dexerto.

claims.claim: Confirmed marriage 21 July with photos captioned 'Mr and MrsBeast'
claims.note: Dexerto caption and date confirmed.

claims.claim: Ceremony on Necker Island, British Virgin Islands; 70 friends and family; no livestreams or YouTube cameras, only a professional photographer
claims.note: Malay Mail, citing People for the location.

claims.claim: Booysen described as South African gamer, author and content creator
claims.note: Matches.

claims.claim: Proposed 25 December 2024; announced engagement 1 January 2025
claims.note: Wikipedia gives both dates. Dexerto confirms a Christmas Day 2024 proposal.

claims.claim: Summary: born Jimmy Donaldson on 7 May 1998 in Wichita, Kansas; American YouTuber; crossed 500 million subscribers on 12 June 2026
claims.note: Now reads "in June 2026". The YouTube blog is dated 12 June 2026 and reports the milestone as already reached, so June 2026 is supported.

claims.claim: FAQ: 28 as of October 2026 (born 7 May 1998)
claims.note: Arithmetic is correct for 2026-10-26.

claims.claim: FAQ: passed 500 million on 12 June 2026, first individual creator
claims.note: Now reads "in June 2026". The YouTube blog is dated 12 June 2026 and reports the milestone as already reached, so June 2026 is supported.

valueNote: Separates platform subscribers, a projected asset figure without an estimator, and annual earnings. Flags company-sourced audience figures and the disputed $5B valuation.
summary: Fixed: the 500M milestone is now dated only to June 2026, which the YouTube blog supports. #TeamTrees now says the campaign aimed to plant 25 million trees. All other claims match the sources. Wikipedia is cited for several facts; the style guide treats it as a research lead only, so consider replacing those citations with primary sources.
